'''Sakura Schafer-Nameki''' is a German [[mathematical physics|mathematical physicist]] working in [[string theory]] and [[supersymmetric gauge theory]].
She works at the [[University of Oxford]] as a Professor of Mathematical Physics in the [[Mathematical Institute, University of Oxford|Mathematical Institute]] and as a senior research fellow of [[Wadham College, Oxford]].{{r|wadham}}

==Early life and education==
Although partly of Japanese descent, Schafer-Nameki is originally from [[Swabia]] in Germany.{{r|gaz}} She studied both physics and mathematics at the [[University of Stuttgart]] from 1995 to 1998. After coming to the [[University of Cambridge]] for the [[Mathematical Tripos]], which she passed with distinction in 1999, she remained at Cambridge for doctoral studies.{{r|cv}} She completed her [[Doctor of Philosophy|Ph.D]]. in 2003; her dissertation, ''D-Branes in Boundary Field Theory'', was supervised by [[Peter Goddard (physicist)|Peter Goddard]].{{r|mg}}

==Career==
After completing her doctorate, Schafer-Nameki became a postdoctoral researcher at the [[University of Hamburg]], a Postdoctoral Prize Fellow at the [[California Institute of Technology]], and a senior postdoctoral fellow at the [[Kavli Institute for Theoretical Physics]]. She took a position as a lecturer at [[King's College London]] in 2010, and was promoted to reader in 2014.{{r|cv}} In 2016 she moved to Oxford as Professor of Mathematical Physics and Tutorial Fellow of Wadham College,{{r|cv|gaz}} becoming a senior research fellow at the college in 2020.{{r|wadham}}

Her research combines [[string theory]] and geometry.<ref name=":0">{{Cite web |title=Our Team |url=https://sites.duke.edu/scshgap/our-team/ |access-date=2022-05-12 |website=Simons Collaboration on Special Holonomy in Geometry, Analysis, and Physics, Duke University |language=en-US}}</ref> She was the principal investigator for the five-year [[European Research Council]] project "Higgs bundles: Supersymmetric Gauge Theories and Geometry" which began in 2016.<ref>{{Cite web |title=ERC Funded Projects |url=https://erc.europa.eu/projects-figures/erc-funded-projects/results?items_per_page=5&f%5B0%5D=call_year%3A2015&f%5B1%5D=tid%253Aparents_all%3A63&f%5B2%5D=funding_scheme%3AConsolidator%20Grant%20%28CoG%29&page=1 |access-date=2022-05-12 |website=European Research Council}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |title=Higgs Bundles: Supersymmetric Gauge Theories and Geometry |url=https://people.maths.ox.ac.uk/schafernamek/ |access-date=2022-05-12 |website=Mathematical Institute, University of Oxford}}</ref> In 2020 she joined the Simons Collaboration on Special Holonomy in Geometry, Analysis, and Physics as one of its Principal Investigators.<ref name=":0" />
